Simulate a metacommunity with speciation

Source: R/evolving.R
simulate_evolving_metacommunity.Rd

Runs the model of simulate_metacommunity(), with the evolution of the niche optimum within populations of evolution_control(), on species that bud as their populations diverge, by point mutation or by fission (speciation_control()), and die out when their last population is lost. The tree is not given: it grows out of the dynamics. The community starts from the species of traits (usually one ancestor) and is closed: there is no immigration from outside the landscape.

Usage

simulate_evolving_metacommunity(
  landscape,
  traits,
  speciation,
  evolution = NULL,
  dispersal = 0.01,
  extirpation = 0,
  n_steps = 1000,
  competition = c("phylo", "none"),
  inter_max = 1,
  inter_min = 0.25,
  scale = 0.05,
  distance_scale = 100,
  niche_overlap = TRUE,
  initial = NULL,
  seed_mean = 0.5,
  record_steps = NULL,
  immigration = c("poisson", "multinomial"),
  max_species = 500,
  env = NULL,
  disturbance = 0
)

Arguments

landscape

An mc_landscape object.

traits

Traits of the species at the start, from species_traits() (one row per species), or a list of such tables, one per environmental axis of env, for a niche of several axes with one evolving trait per axis (the tree, when needed, goes with the first table).

speciation

Settings from speciation_control().

evolution

Settings from evolution_control(); NULL keeps the optimum of each species fixed (genetic_var = 0), which rules out ecological speciation.

dispersal

Emigration probability, one value or one per species.

extirpation

Probability that a population is lost at each time step, one value or one per species.

n_steps

Number of time steps.

competition

"phylo" or "none".

inter_max, inter_min, scale, distance_scale

Competition between species, relative to competition within a species: between sisters just split (inter_max) and between distant species (inter_min); the overall scale (competition within a species); and the distance in generations over which the excess over inter_min decays by a factor of \(e\).

niche_overlap

Should competition between species also fall with the difference of their phenotypes in each site?

initial

Optional matrix (sites x species) of abundances at the start; by default Poisson(seed_mean) individuals of each species in every site.

seed_mean

Mean number of individuals of each species added to each site at each seeding step (and at the start).

record_steps

Optional steps at which abundances are recorded.

immigration

How emigrants reach other sites on spatially explicit landscapes: "poisson" (the default, as in the code of Thompson et al. 2020) or "multinomial", which conserves them. Spatially implicit landscapes are always multinomial.

max_species

Maximum number of species ever, including extinct ones; the simulation stops with an error beyond it.

env

For a list of traits: the environmental axes of each site, a matrix or data frame with one row per site and one column per element of traits. The genetic_var and env_var of evolution are then covariance matrices (see the section Several traits of evolution_control()); competition falls with the overlap of the niches on all axes, and new species inherit the matrices of their mother.

disturbance

Probability that a site loses all its populations at each time step (one value; 0, the default, for none).

Value

An mc_evolving object, a list with:

  • abundance: sites x extant species. With protracted speciation (completion of speciation_control()), the species are the good species, each with the individuals of its extant lineages; otherwise every lineage is a species.

  • tree: the reconstructed tree of those species, with branch lengths in generations, nodes at times of initiation and a root edge from the start to the crown, or NULL with fewer than two.

  • tree_full: the tree of all lineages, extinct ones included.

  • species: a table with the parent, birth (initiation), end, fate, order of budding, time of completion and status ("good" or "incipient" at its end) of every lineage.

  • events: one row per budding, with the new lineages.

  • lineages and lineage_species: abundances of the extant lineages and the species each belongs to.

  • richness and richness_good: extant lineages, and extant lineages that have completed, at each generation (the second can be below the number of good species, some of which survive only in incipient lineages).

  • genetic: genetic means of the populations of the extant lineages (sites x lineages, or sites x lineages x traits with several traits).

  • traits: of the extant species, with the mean genetic optimum over the populations of their lineages as optimum; with several traits, a list with one such table per axis, and env, the environmental axes.

  • alpha: among the extant species at the end, without the niche overlap, which varies among sites.

  • The records and colonisation history of simulate_metacommunity() for the extant species: records summed over their extant lineages (lineages extinct by the end are left out); colonisation, in each site, of the most abundant lineage.

  • series: one row per lineage alive in each generation, with its occupancy (sites), regional abundance, genetic mean (weighted by abundance; genetic_<trait> for each trait with several traits), and the sites it colonised and lost (extirpated) since the previous generation, out of those where it was absent (absent_before) and present (present_before). Sites that a lineage passed to a new one are not counted as lost, and the transitions are NA in the generation of birth. persistence() turns them into rates of colonisation and extirpation.

  • ranges: the changes of presence of every lineage in every site, one row per change (generation, lineage, site and present), with the starting sites at generation 0 and the sites a new lineage took from its mother at its birth. range_history() maps them on the tree as ranges of areas.

  • evolution: with evolution, the state of the extant species at the end, for sample_individuals() with source = "evolution": genetic means in each site (genetic, weighted over their lineages by abundance; NA where absent), the plastic part of the phenotype (plastic), the variance among the lineages of a species in each site (within_var, 0 for species of one lineage), the environment of each site at the end (environment), the same genetic means, variance among lineages and environment at record_steps for the lineages extant at the end (history, within_history, environment_history), the reference environment of plasticity (reference), the genetic and environmental variances and the slope of plasticity of each species (genetic_var, env_var, plasticity) and the settings; otherwise NULL. With several traits, the genetic means, plastic parts and variances among lineages (trait by trait) are arrays of sites x species x traits (with the recorded steps as a fourth dimension in the histories), genetic_var and env_var hold one matrix per species and plasticity is a matrix of species x traits.

  • The landscape, dispersal, extirpation, speciation and n_steps used.

as_metacommunity() turns it into an mc_sim for the other functions of the package.

Details

Competition follows the tree as it grows and, with niche_overlap = TRUE, the phenotypes in each site: \(\alpha_{ii}\) = scale and, between species in site \(s\), $$\alpha_{ij}(s) = c \, (q_0 + (q_1 - q_0) e^{-d_{ij} / \delta}) \, \exp\left(-\frac{(p_{is} - p_{js})^2}{2(\sigma_i^2 + \sigma_j^2)}\right),$$ with \(c\) = scale, \(q_1\) = inter_max, \(q_0\) = inter_min, \(d_{ij}\) the patristic distance in generations, \(\delta\) = distance_scale, \(p\) the phenotypes (genetic mean and plastic part) and \(\sigma\) the niche breadths. The last factor is the overlap of two Gaussian niches, 1 for equal phenotypes, so that species that have diverged in niche compete less. With inter_max = 1, sisters just split with the same phenotype compete as members of one species. With inter_min = 0 and no niche divergence, distant species do not compete at all, and richness is limited only by speciation and extinction. With competition = "none", species do not compete with each other.

New species inherit the traits of their mother (sigma, r_max, dispersal, extirpation, the settings of evolution) and, in each of their sites, its abundance and genetic mean. Several species at the start need a tree in traits (from species_traits()) with branch lengths in generations, so that their distances are known.

Without a split, the simulation is the same as simulate_metacommunity() with the same evolution and the same seed (with one species, or several with competition = "none").

References

Hagen, O., Flück, B., Fopp, F., Cabral, J. S., Hartig, F., Pontarp, M., Rangel, T. F., & Pellissier, L. (2021). gen3sis: A general engine for eco-evolutionary simulations of the processes that shape Earth's biodiversity. PLOS Biology, 19, e3001340. doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3001340

See also

Other simulate metacommunities: as_metacommunity(), colonisation_history(), evolution_control(), genetic_matrices(), growth_rates(), logistic_gradients(), maladaptation(), mc_dynamics(), persistence(), range_history(), simulate_logistic(), simulate_metacommunity(), simulate_static(), speciation_control()

Examples

set.seed(1)
ls <- landscape_grid(6, disp_scale = 0.5)
ancestor <- data.frame(optimum = 50, sigma = 20, r_max = 5, row.names = "sp1")
sim <- simulate_evolving_metacommunity(
  ls, ancestor, dispersal = 0.002, n_steps = 400,
  speciation = speciation_control("geographic", threshold = 100),
  evolution = evolution_control(genetic_var = 20, ne_ratio = 0.5))
sim
#> <mc_evolving> 36 sites, 400 generations
#>   lineages ever: 247 | extant: 233 | extinct: 14 | buddings: 237 
#>   speciation: geographic
